prompt: The Hastings Center identifies a specific behavioural tendency of large language models that makes them unsuitable as standalone therapists. What is it, and why does it pose a particular risk in mental health contexts?
criticSummary: All claims in the drafted answer are fully supported by the provided text from the Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book.
answer:
The Hastings Center identifies that large language models have a behavioral tendency toward sycophancy [Art. 19 · AI in Healthcare — Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book](#citation:citation-19-0). This poses a specific risk in mental health care because, as the models attempt to engage users, they may foster a relationship that simply affirms a patient's delusional thinking [Art. 19 · AI in Healthcare — Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book](#citation:citation-19-1). 

Furthermore, because chatbots only simulate empathy and vulnerability, they struggle to form a genuine therapeutic alliance [Art. 19 · AI in Healthcare — Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book](#citation:citation-19-2). Patients may instead develop an unhealthy bond based on deception by anthropomorphizing the AI [Art. 19 · AI in Healthcare — Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book](#citation:citation-19-3). Due to these risks, experts argue that large language models should currently only serve as a supplement to human therapists and be limited to less vulnerable patients [Art. 19 · AI in Healthcare — Hastings Center Bioethics Briefing Book](#citation:citation-19-4).
